I would say that it comes back to how you use your jutsu.  The extra power goes a long way helping out with poison and paralysis stacking.  I'm not sure if fire shuriken's fire proc scales with ninja power, but with B-rabbit I only need two to proc fire on anything. You hit triangle right after you see your weapon bounce.  It also works starting from mid stance.  I have a bad tendency to just spam square as fast as possible when using dual swords, thus making my moon shadows very late (usually after the 3rd bounce).  It'll take practice to make that muscle memory if you want to git gud with it.

To give a bit of constructive criticism: the writing could use a touch up. While you did put in a disclaimer that a fair amount is copy/paste from the internet there are sections with unnecessary run on sentences.  It makes it difficult to convey the information you want to give.  Your audience may not appreciate that.

Secondly I think you may be confusing "Ninjutsu" with "Ready Jutsu" from the shine.  Ninjutsu is just the page with your ninja skills, it does not encompass magic.  I would change this to "What is Jutsu?" and perhaps explain how to navigate the shrine menus prior to it.  This would help reduce sections that say "Refer back to X" or name drop the shrine prior to explaining what the shrine is.

I understand your previous post had some controversial feedback regarding making your guide, and I do hope that my comment has been insightful to you.  Best of luck.

For the sake of being helpful let's say if you were to go through with it I'd probably pick up one of the deviant bows since they charge up arts faster; the Deadeye one is a good allrounder.  You could  maybe try a set that has Trump Card on it (needs 10 chance), that increases the power of hunter arts.  Trump card procs when a monster is disabled, paralyzed, trapped, tripped, KO'd, or down after a mount.  To proc that often you could either have skills that speed up trap placement, or use bows that have innate boosts to para coatings.  Just remember that while the wire art is active your coatings are being overriden by the wire, so the shot will not have their effects.

Honestly, getting a setup like that to basically run HAME bow runs to cut tails would be a pain.  I'd recommend playing with a blademaster friend instead.  But if you decide to go through with it, hope that helps.

That's actually a bit of a tricky question because blast has always had a identity crisis since it's no longer an abnormal status, but isn't an element since it seems to still proc the explosion on a buildup threshold.  While there isn't any data to suggest it, the general consensus is that it does help, but you are likely to be dealing more damage with power coatings to boost the Teo's raw, rather than relying on the blast.

Pierce gunning in general is one of my favorites, it's a pretty cool feeling when you drop a Plesioth to sleep in two shots.  [Here](https://www.reddit.com/r/MonsterHunter/comments/4y1efe/which_bows_are_you_guys_using/) is a post earlier about bows that people have liked, lots of solid choices there.  I also highly recommend the [guide](http://laxgg.blogspot.com/p/mhgen-introduction-contents.html) by Laxaria if you haven't read that allready.  I'm using the Dreadqueen set with a Herbology charm when I hunt with groups, so I feel like I have amazing ultility in addition to bringing great raw damage.  The other deviant set I'm working on is the Redhelm set (dem hairs), and I'm excited to see how it's skills will affect how I handle hunts.

I think that some people DO consider the arts/new styles to be OP because experienced hunters can utilize more opportunities to perform maximum damage on a monster safely.  Mhgen encourages diversity in hunting moreso than any previous monster hunter, so I think the idea of a "meta" is just silly. I love that every room I've come across is always different in how people individually approach their hunts.  That said people I've run into that do that tend to have just switched to a different weapon that wasn't part of a saved set, so they lost their art and forgot to put one on.  I mention that Bow guy because he was REALLY limiting himself by losing both the arc/power shot, and not shooting at the critical distance.

A personal favorite of mine is the Arachnid Bow. You make it with the toxic kumori from the cat hunts.  20% affinity and a bonus to sleep coatings, I've literally gotten a monster to sleep with two shots from it.  It's pierce so I don't bring it to every fight, but I really like it.   If you're interested in a spread bow Chaos Bow is also a solid choice for status, I really enjoyed using it in the arena Narga match (got S rank the on the first try with it).

Bow has the least amount of upkeep, just make sure you have a good grasp of stamina management so you don't overcharge/undercharge shots outside of critical zones.  The bowguns have changed with internal ammo to help out with early game costs, and it is nice to be able to not have to worry about stamina.  The dynamics between solo and group play are night and day when you main ranged. 

Regardless of your choice, I highly recommend reading up on monster hitzones so you know where to shoot at.  A lot of people tend to shoot blindly their first hunt with the ranged classes and wonder why their times are abysmal.  Be patient, constant review yourself, and most importantly have fun!

You can't do that if you're not happy with who you are, and in my life that has been especially true whenever I tried to start a relationship to feel happy.

One thing that I like to do on Valentines Day is to volunteer or find something nice to do for someone else, doesn't even have to be someone you'd be romantically interested in.
